conditions: Holders of ordinary passports, listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 as applied by Spain
Stay counts across the whole Schengen area, not Spain alone
Must meet Schengen entry conditions at the border, including proof of sufficient financial means (2026: 122 EUR per person per day, minimum 1,099 EUR for stays of 9 days or more)
GBR row covers British citizens; other British nationality classes (BN(O), BOTC, BOC, BPP, BS) are separately visa-exempt under Annex II Part 3
Listed in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 as applied by Spain

Annex II footnote: 'The exemption from the visa requirement shall apply from the date of entry into force of an agreement on visa exemption to be concluded with the European Union' (the EU-UAE short-stay visa-waiver agreement is in application; see unresolved)
Exemption applies only to holders of a 'Hong Kong Special Administrative Region' passport (Annex II, Section 2)
Exemption applies only to holders of a 'Regiao Administrativa Especial de Macau' passport (Annex II, Section 2)
Exemption applies only to holders of passports issued by Taiwan which include an identity card number (Annex II, Section 4)

EU citizens: freedom of movement. 'Citizens of the European Union, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland may enter and travel within Spain with their national identity document or with their valid passport'
No visa and no 90/180 short-stay visa-policy cap; EU residence rules apply for stays beyond 3 months
Listed in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806: a Schengen short-stay (type C) visa is required for tourism
Apply through the Spanish consulate competent for the applicant's place of residence; in many jurisdictions lodgement is in person by appointment at the authorized BLS Spain Visa Application Center
Must apply from the country of residence or origin (e.g. Washington consulate: holders of US B1/B2 visas 'must apply for a visa in their country of residence or country of origin')

All nationalities in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 (including, among others, Vanuatu, whose exemption was suspended) require a Schengen short-stay visa obtained in advance from a Spanish consulate / authorized visa application center

No tourist visa needed for stays up to 90 days in any 180-day period (Annex II exemption or EU freedom of movement); a national (type D) visa applies only to long stays, which are out of scope for tourism

Spain operates no tourist eVisa. Official channel set per MFA/consulate pages: visa-exempt entry (Annex II) or a Schengen visa applied for in person by appointment at the consulate / authorized BLS visa application center

As of 2026-07-23 no travel authorization is required: ETIAS 'is expected to become operational in the last quarter of 2026' (Spanish MFA) / 'will be mandatory from the last quarter of 2026' (spain.info). Once live it will apply to visa-exempt third-country nationals
Spain operates no visa-on-arrival program for tourism. Official pages require visa-obliged nationals to obtain the Schengen visa in advance, in person by appointment, before travel

policies.policy_name: Schengen visa-exemption list applied by Spain (Annex II, Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, consolidated 03.02.2025)
policies.description: Nationals of Annex II states, the Chinese SARs and listed entities are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area, for tourism among other non-gainful purposes. Published by the Spanish MFA (Washington consulate) as 'Lista paises obligados y exentos de visado Schengen 2025'. Also exempt: British nationals who are not British citizens (BN(O), BOTC, BOC, BPP, BS) under Annex II Part 3.
conditions: Hong Kong SAR: 'Hong Kong Special Administrative Region' passport holders only
Macao SAR: 'Regiao Administrativa Especial de Macau' passport holders only
Taiwan: passports including an identity card number only
Kosovo: biometric passports issued in line with ICAO standards only
Georgia, Moldova, Ukraine: biometric passports issued in line with ICAO standards only
North Macedonia, Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro: biometric passports only

Several states (e.g. United Arab Emirates, Dominica, Micronesia, Grenada, Kiribati, Saint Lucia, and footnote-3 states such as Peru, Palau, Marshall Islands, Nauru, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Tuvalu, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines): exemption applies from entry into force of a visa-exemption agreement with the European Union
Entry subject to Schengen Borders Code conditions, including proof of sufficient financial means (2026: 122 EUR per person per day, minimum 1,099 EUR for stays of 9 days or more)

policies.policy_name: Schengen short-stay (type C) visa via Spanish consulates and BLS visa application centers
policies.description: Nationals listed in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806 need a Schengen visa to travel to Spain for tourism. Applications are lodged in person, by appointment, at the Spanish consulate competent for the applicant's residence or at its authorized BLS Spain Visa Application Center. The visa allows up to 90 days in any 180-day period in the Schengen area for tourism, business, family visits, medical treatment, studies, non-work internships or volunteer activities.
conditions: Application in person by appointment only
Apply in country of residence or origin

Passport valid at least 90 days (3 months) beyond expected departure from the Schengen area, issued within the previous 10 years, with at least two blank visa pages (application requirement at Washington consulate)
